newsitem.title: UK: Shortcovering rallies IPE Brent at close.
newsitem.headline: Shortcovering rallies IPE Brent at close.

text.p: Sharp losses on NYMEX kept IPE Brent under pressure in late trade, but shortcovering rallied the market into the close, brokers said.

Brent was languishing in late trade as the weaker U.S. markets saw profit-taking trim recent gains fuelled by Middle East tension and low distillate stocks, but underlying bull sentiment saw shortcovering pull it back from the lows.
The November Brent contract last traded 40 cents down at $21.91 a barrel after finding support at $21.80.
"Sentiment is bullish and the market volatile, people took their profits then covered back the shorts," a broker said.
Dealers said both gas oil and Brent fell in fairly light volume on profit-taking in the absence of fresh news.

The fundamental outlook is still seen as positive with heating oil and diesel stocks running well below year-ago levels on both sides of the Atlantic and winter approaching, traders expect the market to remain firm in the longer term.

News that the United States moved a second aircraft carrier into the Gulf and flew more troops to Kuwait on Thursday in a military buildup aimed at deterring any threat from Iraq caused few ripples in the market.
